transcript:
Meeting header: 
- Date/Time: Tue Jun 23 2026 15:00 PDT
- Duration: 47 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Kapoor (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood SA); Elena Ruiz (CTO, StratusLogic), Martin Gao (Eng Mgr), Priya Singh (Cloud Architect), Tom O'Neal (Security)

Topics: marketplace listing checklist, VPC connector networking, KMS/HSM compatibility, quantization and performance tradeoffs, pilot success criteria

--- Optional auto-summary (auto-generated):
Redwood explained listing requirements and private deployment patterns; StratusLogic raised questions about KMS integration, egress costs, and canary routing for dedicated vs hosted options. Agreed to run a short throughput/latency benchmark and exchange packaging artifacts.

[00:00] Maya: okay welcome everyone thanks for doing this, uh we wanted to make sure we cover the listing prep plus the private/vpc connector details, so i'll hand to ravi for the technical primer in a minute but quick round robin intros?
[00:18] Elena: yeah this is Elena from stratuslogic, CTO, we run their analytics stack, we're curious about how Redwood would appear on the marketplace and what private deploy means for our compliance constraints
[00:29] Martin: Martin here, engineering manager, we'll own the integration work and the pilot rings
[00:34] Priya: Priya, cloud architect, i'll be mapping network and identity flows
[00:41] Tom: Tom, security. interested in KMS, audit logs, and data residency options
[00:45] Maya: great thanks, ravi?
[00:49] Ravi: thanks, um quick agenda: 1) marketplace packaging requirements and what we need from you; 2) private deployment patterns (vpc peering, onprem connector, helm chart); 3) KMS/HSM and audit trail details; 4) perf/quant tradeoffs and pilot scope. we'll leave time for Qs and next steps
[01:05] Maya: also want to note we usually recommend a tiny pilot with our dedicated or private runtime so customers can hit their latency/throughput SLOs before full listing
[01:12] Elena: good. what does listing actually require? we saw the doc but want to confirm artifacts
[01:17] Ravi: yeah so the marketplace package is a bundle: helm chart + values preview, a minimal deployment manifest for our onprem operator, a security matrix (sso, scim, roles), and an ops runbook. we provide a sample helm values file for both marketplace and onprem. i'll attach the checklist after this call (link: https://redwood.example/partner-packaging-checklist)
[01:42] Priya: does that include KMS integration details? we use GCP KMS for keys but some teams want HSM-backed keys in the future
[01:48] Ravi: good question. for private we support KMS integration via our connector. we have documented integrations for AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and Vault HSM. note: the marketplace listing requires a statement of supported key managers and recommended config. for HSM we have a compatibility note — some HSM drivers need privileged mounts in the helm chart
[02:10] Tom: when you say 'privileged mounts' that raises flags for our security team, can you avoid hostPath usage?
[02:16] Lena: typically we avoid hostPath. for HSM we prefer exposing PKCS#11 over a sidecar and supporting mTLS to the HSM proxy so the chart can be non-privileged in many platforms. it'll be in the runbook
[02:30] Martin: network topology: we use a dedicated VPC per environment, with private peering to partner services. what are your network requirements? ports, TLS, egress?
[02:39] Ravi: minimal ports: 443 outbound for control plane, 443 inbound from the marketplace registry when installing; inside cluster we use gRPC on configurable port (default 5100) and a sidecar for metrics on 9100. egress patterns depend on whether you use hosted model artifacts or host the model bits in your registry — if you pull model weights from our hosted store you'll see heavier egress
[03:02] Priya: we plan to host models on our registry to avoid cross-region egress. any gotchas?
[03:08] Ravi: if models are local you avoid remote egress. caveat: you need to ensure the runtime has the correct KV cache persistence and the filesystem layout matches our expected path. we'll give a sample init container that lays out weights. also quantized artifacts may need different extensions, so please make sure your OCI registry preserves content-type metadata
[03:35] Elena: can you explain the routing options in the marketplace listing? like can we offer both hosted and private variants under one listing?
[03:42] Maya: yes you can. we support a multi-variant listing: hosted API, dedicated reserved capacity, and private deploy. the marketplace listing doc has fields for supported variants and recommended default. many customers list multiple SKUs. but note pricing and SLA granularity differ
[03:58] Tom: audit logs — we'll need immutable audit trails sent to our SIEM for regulatory reasons. does Redwood expose logs via syslog or push to customer Splunk?
[04:08] Ravi: we support forwarders to common sinks: syslog, Splunk HEC, S3-compatible archives. for private we can route audit logs to a customer-owned bucket and encrypt at rest with your KMS key. the listing needs a section describing retention and export options
[04:27] Priya: okay good. what about SSO and RBAC — we use SAML and OIDC, and need SCIM provisioning
[04:34] Lena: we support SAML SSO, OIDC, and SCIM provisioning. the marketplace package includes a sample SSO metadata and SCIM provisioning manifest. if you require SCIM attribute mapping we'll work with you on the mapping table
[04:49] Martin: all right, pilot: performance. we want to validate 100 concurrent sessions with p95 latency under 300ms for short-chat flows (~128 tokens). what's realistic?
[04:59] Ravi: depends on model size and quantization. for a 13B model quantized to int8 on our dedicated tier, hitting p95 ~200-250ms for 128-token exchange is plausible with a steady batching config and warm KV cache. if you plan to run in private on smaller hardware we can provide a perf matrix. i'll share a harness (k6 script + sample prompt set)
[05:25] Elena: how much variance should we expect during cold starts? our UX team cares a lot about that initial burst
[05:30] Ravi: cold starts can be 2-6x latency depending on model weights and cache priming. we recommend warming hooks — we provide an init-warm job that runs on deploy and we can pre-populate KV cache from snapshots if you want fast 99s
[05:45] Tom: regarding data residency, we need guaranteed residency in eu-west-1 for customer data keys. can private deploy handle that?
[05:53] Maya: yes, private can be deployed in your VPC in eu-west-1. we also support a private control plane option where metadata stays in your tenancy. for the listing please mark the supported regions
[06:05] Priya: KMS key access: do you need cross-account IAM roles? I want to avoid giving wide permissions
[06:12] Ravi: we recommend a least-privilege role scoped to decrypt/encrypt for the specific key. for GCP we prefer a service account with kms.cryptoKeyVersions.use permission on the key ring. we can provide a sample IAM policy
[06:26] Martin: are there any known issues with our ingress controller (we use contour) and your sidecars?
[06:32] Lena: contour should be fine; we test with ingress-nginx and contour. you might need to tweak proxy-protocol for gRPC passthrough. we'll include a contour values snippet in the package
[06:45] Elena: on quantization: we saw notes about accuracy regressions — how do we evaluate quality tradeoffs?
[06:52] Ravi: Redwood Optimize recommends quant profiles by workload; we tie quality monitoring to prompt evaluation sets. for the pilot we ask you to share 200 representative prompts so we can compute regression deltas across model/quant combos. we also support bespoke eval hooks if you want server-side scoring
[07:12] Priya: network egress monitoring — do you emit token-level cost telemetry? our finance team wants to understand unit economics
[07:19] Maya: in Redwood Console we provide token-level cost estimates and per-route breakdowns. for private deployments we can ship an exporter that logs token counts and aggregates to your preferred metrics backend
[07:33] Tom: security review: do you have SOC 2 and what levels of pen testing?
[07:39] Maya: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II. we do regular pen tests and can share a whitepaper and pen-test summary under an NDA. we'll put those links in the follow-up pack
[07:52] Elena: competitors — we looked at CloudGreek and BigLakeAI; any features we should be aware of that differ?
[07:59] Ravi: two quick diffs: CloudGreek focuses on single-tenant appliance models with less flexible routing; BigLakeAI emphasizes a serverless approach but less deterministic latency SLAs. Redwood's differentiator is the unified runtime plus predictable routing + marketplace listing workflow
[08:20] Martin: question about upgrades — how do model rollouts happen? we want canaries
[08:25] Lena: our rollout system supports canary percent-based rollouts and automatic rollback on regressions tied to eval sets. for private you can control rollout via our operator or use console-driven policies if you expose the control-plane endpoint to Redwood
[08:40] Priya: control-plane exposure is a non-starter for our security. can we do fully air-gapped onprem?
[08:46] Ravi: fully air-gapped is supported with our onprem bundle, but some features like hosted telemetry and auto-update won't be available. we provide an offline packaging process and an upgrade bundle you can apply manually
[09:02] Elena: sample artifacts you mentioned — can you list what you'll share after the call?
[09:08] Maya: sure: 1) packaging checklist + sample helm values; 2) VPC connector runbook + contour/ingress snippets; 3) KMS/IAM sample policies; 4) perf test harness (k6 + prompt set template); 5) SOC 2 and pen test summary (NDA). links will be sent in follow-up email
[09:29] Martin: for the pilot timeline — we want a 2-week integration sprint then a 1-week perf run. is that realistic?
[09:36] Ravi: yes that's a typical cadence if you can allocate an eng lead to the work. week 1 for deploy + config, week 2 for functional tests and warm-up, week 3 perf and stability tests. we'll help run the perf experiments remotely
[09:52] Priya: any specific kernel/hardware needs for the private runtime? we might use on-prem servers with A100s or mix of T4s in our dev stack
[09:59] Ravi: for low-latency workloads we recommend either A100 or H100 for large models; T4s can work for smaller quantized setups. we'll send a hardware-perf spreadsheet. also note CUDA and driver compat — we pin supported driver versions in chart notes
[10:17] Tom: compliance question: do you retain prompts/outputs by default? retention policy?
[10:23] Lena: by default we keep minimal request metadata for debugging, but retention is configurable. for private you set retention policies in the operator values; we can default to zero-retention for stored content and forward telemetry only
[10:37] Elena: what about billing for marketplace listing? do we handle metering for private deploys?
[10:44] Maya: private deployments are typically under an enterprise contract; the marketplace listing can display a contact-sales CTA. for dedicated we have metering and reserved capacity models. for private we offer both subscription + usage add-ons; billing integration depends on the marketplace (some marketplaces support metering hooks)
[10:59] Martin: if we want to run a canary that routes 10% to Redwood hosted and 90% to private, is that supported?
[11:07] Ravi: yes our smart routing supports policy-based routing by region/tier/variant. you can do 10% hosted fallback and automatic retry. keep in mind egress/cost implications for the hosted fraction
[11:20] Priya: any blocking items we should get to you asap?
[11:24] Maya: the main blockers: network topology, KMS access model, and pilot perf targets. if you share those we'll scope the pilot properly
[11:31] Elena: we'll aim to send topology + perf targets by 6/30
[11:35] Maya: perfect. next steps recap: we'll send artifacts and a proposed pilot runbook, you provide diagrams and perf goals, we schedule a kickoff once we have those
[11:46] Tom: one more on security — can you provide an example of least-privilege IAM and a short threat model doc?
[11:52] Lena: yes we'll include an example IAM policy and a 2-page threat model for private deploys
[11:58] Martin: timeline question — can we be marketplace-ready in 4-6 weeks?
[12:03] Maya: with a focused pilot and no major infra blockers, 4-6 weeks is feasible. If air-gapped or HSM needs arise it adds time for validation
[12:15] Elena: thanks all, useful. we'll review the materials and follow up.
[12:20] Maya: thanks everyone, i'll send the checklist and links; ravi will follow up on perf harness. closing now.

--- End of transcript.
